svg.title: PCB sublimation press stack and edge taping
svg.desc: Schematic cross-section, not to scale. Heat comes from above. Transfer ink touches white top mask directly. The rigid PCB sits on fresh blowout paper and one firm silicone lower pad. A separate plan shows the 100 by 150 millimeter top face with current jig-hole centers and four tape tabs outside the artwork.

g.text: TOP-ONLY SUBLIMATION / PRESS SETUP
First printed coupon: 185 °C / 365 °F · 60 s · LIGHT pressure · WARM peel at about 40–50 °C
Selected trial settings; no machine run or Mechanic mask qualification claimed.
Cross-section / schematic, thicknesses exaggerated
Heated upper platen
Optional THIN PTFE / Teflon cover
Fresh absorbent blowout paper
Transfer paper / INK SIDE DOWN
White top solder mask / receiving face
Rigid FR4 / 1.5 mm board thickness
Bottom copper + white mask / pads open
Fresh protective blowout paper
ONE smooth, firm silicone support pad
Flat lower platen / continuous support
INK TOUCHES MASK DIRECTLY
No PTFE, protective paper or silicone between ink and mask.
No jig, pins, tape/CA bond or stuffed garment pillow in the press.
Cold taping / plan schematic
100 × 150 mm top / Y down on this page
TRANSFER INK
AGAINST WHITE TOP
Four edge tabs
outside printed detail
Blue dashed: handling margin in paper.
Gold: heat-tape tabs to board edge/back.
Green: existing jig holes / no press pins.
Add edge strips only if lifting occurs;
leave corner vents. Do not trap moisture.
Open slowly → keep transfer taped while cooling → peel up and away without sliding.
Inspect BOTH coatings after this one heat cycle. Record pad, cover, tape pattern, pressure-knob position and peel delay.
